findings.title: --full text render drops an uncited twin-named workstream (missed kind+name site)
findings.recommendation: citedNames is name-only (add(entry.name); standalone filters !citedNames.has(w.name)) — with change 'alpha' cited to a stage and staging explore 'alpha' uncited, the explore is silently omitted from the --full TEXT view (neither nested nor standalone), violating the standalone-listing rule and the per-workstream cold-start mandate. JSON is unaffected (dumps workstreams directly), capping severity. This is the one comparison site the iter-2 'identity is kind+name everywhere' resolution missed. Track printed entries by kind:name key (or object identity) and filter standalone against that; add the cited-twin fixture.

findings.title: Generated bodies still direct bare `orbit status --json` for per-change gate payloads
findings.recommendation: Three sites in apply-change.ts (:138 position-readout convention, :228 no-chunking rule, :266 completion-prompt override) and one in archive-change.ts (:193 guardrail) still say bare `orbit status --json` where the per-change gate payload is meant. Post-D3, bare --json returns the orientation shape {sprint, last, next, also, waiting} — no top-level position/gates — and in a multi-change repo the sprint may be a DIFFERENT change, so a literal reader records the wrong change's position/next in emits. The orbit-engine-gates delta scoped exactly this reference class in the SPECS; the template layer wasn't swept (change-completeness residue). Scope all four to `orbit status --change <name> --json`, rebuild + update --force, re-pin the orbit-apply-change/orbit-archive-change parity hashes.

findings.title: Two spec phrasings, one render, for the empty-last line
findings.recommendation: Fault-isolation clause (a) says an all-invalid trail's 'last reports no readable emits' while the continuity emit-less scenario says 'last reports no emits yet'; the implementation renders 'no emits yet' in both cases (readValidEmits cannot distinguish never-emitted from all-invalid, and 'no emits yet' is strictly false when unreadable files exist). Before the letter fixes into baseline: unify the spec on one phrase, or render 'no readable emits' when .json files were present but none survived validation.
